title: Mixtral of Experts
hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.
key_points: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts: 8 feed-forward experts per layer, a learned router picks 2 per token, giving ~47B total params but ~13B active params per forward pass.
Matches or beats Llama 2 70B on most benchmarks while using roughly half the compute per token.
Released under Apache 2.0 with open weights, making a large-capacity MoE accessible to the community.
Builds on Mistral 7B's grouped-query and sliding-window attention, extending it to the MoE setting.
content_html: Mistral AI published Mixtral 8x7B in January 2024, an open-weights sparse Mixture-of-Experts model built on top of the Mistral 7B architecture. The key structural choice — 8 expert feed-forward networks per transformer layer with only 2 activated per token — gives the model a large parameter count while keeping the per-token compute budget modest.
extra_html:
How it works

Each transformer layer contains 8 feed-forward networks (the experts) and a small router network. For every token, the router scores all 8 experts and selects the top 2; the token is processed by just those two, and their outputs are combined. This means the model has roughly 47 billion total parameters but uses only around 13 billion for any single token, similar in cost to a dense 13B model.

Why it matters

Mixtral demonstrated that sparse MoE scaling works in practice for open releases, not just at proprietary labs like Google (Switch Transformer). Matching Llama 2 70B quality at half the active-parameter cost is a meaningful efficiency gain for anyone running inference. The Apache 2.0 license made it one of the most capable freely usable models at its release. Read the paper on arXiv.
